rows.title: Referential integrity bugs related to catalog, basket, and order
rows.excerpt:
Hi,

There appears to be code logic that breaks referential integrity constraints and causes inconsistencies during execution. I would like to share this to understand if the issues are valid in the context of the application, and whether these bugs could be addressed. Thank you in advance.

The issues are related to the data associations established across the catalog, basket, and order microservices, where the baskets and orders contain item IDs that reference the item IDs of the corresponding products in the catalog.

Below are the steps to reproduce the bugs and their potential impact on the system.

### Scenario 1: Catalog-Basket

**Steps to reproduce bugs:**

Consider a client that manages its cart items via the Web App and an administrator who manages the catalog via the REST API.

The flow of requests is illustrated in a shared [figure](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tvxXGYsScQAVJruN8ydk3aSRd-IpnS0r/view?usp=sharing). The illustrated databases contain data from the original application. For simplicity, only the catalog and basket services are represented, along with the most relevant calls and arguments.

- The client adds items to the basket. _(fig. calls 1-3)_
- The admin lists all items from the catalog to get the IDs of the items. _(fig. calls 4-5)_
- The admin deletes an item from the catalog. _(fig. calls 6-7)_
- The client proceeds to the checkout. _(fig. calls 8-12)_

**Description of the bugs:**

**1. Absence of cascading delete:** each basket item contains the ID of the corresponding catalog item, resembling a foreign key. However, when the catalog item is deleted (fig. call 7), this action is not propagated to the basket, leaving a reference that is no longer valid.

During checkout (or even when viewing the cart), the web app's [`FetchBasketItemsAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/blob/1b2698cd83ed5c9e00a2fa954f2586c87022c431/src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs#L117) receives data from querying the basket (fig. calls 9-10, where the returned item IDs contain the deleted item ID) that is inconsistent with the data obtained from querying the catalog (fig. calls 11-12, where the returned items do not contain the deleted item).

The web app's [`FetchBasketItemsAsync`](https://github.com/dotnet/eShop/blob/1b2698cd83ed5c9e00a2fa954f2586c87022c431/src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs#L117)  expects that every basket item is present in the ret

rows.title: Insecure file-serving pattern: `GetItemPictureById` allows path traversal / arbitrary file read via `PictureFileName'
rows.excerpt:
## Summary

`Catalog.API`'s product-image endpoint builds a filesystem path by concatenating a **database-stored, client-controllable** `PictureFileName` directly into `Path.Combine(..., "Pics", pictureFileName)` and streams the result with `TypedResults.PhysicalFile`, with no containment check. Because `Path.Combine` lets a rooted or `..`-containing final segment escape the `Pics` directory, a caller can make the endpoint return **arbitrary files from the host filesystem** (e.g. `appsettings.json`, project source, `/etc/passwd`).

Since this is a **reference application** that many developers copy patterns from, the file-serving idiom here teaches an insecure practice (CWE-22). The fix is small and self-contained.

## Affected code

`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs`

```csharp
// GetItemPictureById (~line 205) — PictureFileName comes from the stored CatalogItem
var path = GetFullPath(environment.ContentRootPath, item.PictureFileName);
...
return TypedResults.PhysicalFile(path, mimetype, lastModified: lastModified);

// ~line 420
public static string GetFullPath(string contentRootPath, string pictureFileName) =>
    Path.Combine(contentRootPath, "Pics", pictureFileName);   // <-- no normalization / containment
```

`PictureFileName` is bound straight from the request body in `CreateItem`/`UpdateItem` (`product.PictureFileName`), so it is fully attacker-controlled.

## Steps to reproduce



**Observed scope:** any real on-disk file the process can read is returned. (`/proc/*` pseudo-files are *not* returned — `PhysicalFile` reports `Content-Length: 0` for procfs and Kestrel aborts the response — so process environment variables are not exfiltrable through this particular sink.)

## Impact

Unrestricted local file read of the `Catalog.API` host: `appsettings*.json`, mounted secret files, K8s service-account tokens (`/var/run/secrets/...`), data-protection keys, application source, etc. In the default topology `Catalog.API` is an internal service, so realistic exposure requires it to be network-reachable (direct exposure, misconfiguration, or via SSRF/lateral movement) — but the file-read defect itself is unconditional.

## Suggested fix

Constrain the filename to the `Pics` directory. Either reduce it to a bare filename, or verify the resolved path stays inside the base:

rows.title: Reserve catalog stock when an order is validated
rows.excerpt:
## Problem
#732 
#888 
When the Catalog handles `OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidationIntegrationEvent` it only reads `AvailableStock` and compares it to the ordered units. The stock is removed later, when `OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEvent` arrives. Between those two points nothing holds the stock, so several orders for the same last units can all be confirmed and paid. The later ones then hit `RemoveStock`, which either throws on empty stock or silently removes fewer units than were ordered.

## Change

- **Validation** now checks and decrements stock in a single conditional `UPDATE` per item (`WHERE AvailableStock >= units`), so the database decides who gets the last units. It is all or nothing per order: if one item is short, the decrements for the other items are rolled back and the order is rejected.
- **New `StockReservation` table** (migration `AddStockReservation`), one row per order with a status (reserved, committed, released) and the items held. The primary key on `OrderId` keeps a redelivered event from taking stock twice.
- **Cancellation**: the Catalog now subscribes to `OrderStatusChangedToCancelledIntegrationEvent` and returns the reserved stock once. This also covers payment failure, since Ordering cancels the order in that case.
- **Paid** only marks the reservation as committed. Orders validated before this change have no reservation, so their stock is still removed at payment as before.
- The stock change, the reservation and the outgoing confirm/reject event are saved in one local transaction.

## Behaviour changes

- An order containing a product id that does not exist is now rejected. Previously that item was skipped and the order confirmed.
- Available stock drops when the order is validated rather than when it is paid.
- An order cancelled before its validation event is handled leaves a released marker, so the late validation reserves nothing and publishes nothing.

## Not addressed

- Reservations do not expire. An order stuck between validation and payment holds its stock until it is paid or cancelled.
- The RabbitMQ event bus acks a message even when its handler throws, so a failed cancellation is not retried and its stock stays reserved.
- `CatalogItem.RemoveStock` no longer has callers (`AddStock` already had none). Both are left in place.

## Testing

Added `StockReservationTests` to `Catalog

rows.title: Replace .WithX OpenAPI annotations with XML documentation comments in Catalog.API
rows.excerpt:
## Summary

This PR replaces all fluent OpenAPI annotation methods (`.WithSummary()`, `.WithDescription()`, `.WithTags()`, etc.) in `CatalogApi.cs` with equivalent XML documentation comments on the handler methods. This change enables OpenAPI documentation generation from XML doc comments rather than fluent API annotations, following the aspnet-openapi-xml approach.

## Changes Made

### 🗑️ Removed Fluent API Annotations
- Removed all `.WithSummary()`, `.WithDescription()`, `.WithTags()`, and `.WithName()` calls from 19 endpoint mappings
- Simplified endpoint registrations to clean, chainable-free syntax

### 📝 Added XML Documentation
- Added XML `<summary>` and `<remarks>` tags to all 16 handler methods
- Extracted 2 inline lambda methods (`GetCatalogTypes`, `GetCatalogBrands`) into proper named methods with XML documentation
- Preserved existing parameter descriptions using `[Description]` attributes

### Before
```csharp
v1.MapGet("/items", GetAllItemsV1)
    .WithName("ListItems")
    .WithSummary("List catalog items")
    .WithDescription("Get a paginated list of items in the catalog.")
    .WithTags("Items");
```

### After
```csharp
v1.MapGet("/items", GetAllItemsV1);

/// <summary>List catalog items</summary>
/// <remarks>Get a paginated list of items in the catalog.</remarks>
[ProducesResponseType<ProblemDetails>(StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest, "application/problem+json")]
public static async Task<Ok<PaginatedItems<CatalogItem>>> GetAllItemsV1(...)
```

## Validation

✅ **0** remaining `.WithX` calls (all removed)  
✅ **16** XML summary and remarks tags added (one for each method)  
✅ **19** simplified endpoint mappings  
✅ **No functional changes** - all routing, parameters, and behavior preserved

## Benefits

- 🎯 **Centralized Documentation**: OpenAPI docs now generated directly from method XML comments
- 🧹 **Cleaner Code**: Simplified endpoint mappings without fluent chaining
- 📚 **Better IntelliSense**: XML docs provide better IDE support for developers
- 🔄 **Future-Proof**: Aligns with modern ASP.NET Core OpenAPI best practices

This change maintains full backward compatibility while improving the developer experience and documentation approach.

rows.title: Fix KeyNotFoundException and NullReferenceException when catalog items are deleted
rows.excerpt:
When catalog items are deleted, basket items and orders retain references to non-existent product IDs, causing the WebApp to crash with `KeyNotFoundException` during basket operations and the Catalog API to crash with `NullReferenceException` during order validation.

## Changes

**BasketState.cs**
- Replace dictionary indexer with `TryGetValue()` to handle missing catalog items
- Filter out basket items for deleted products instead of crashing
- Add warning log when skipping items

**OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidationIntegrationEventHandler.cs**
- Handle null catalog items during order validation
- Treat deleted products as out of stock to reject orders gracefully
- Add warning log for missing products

## Example

Before:
```csharp
var catalogItem = catalogItems[item.ProductId]; // throws KeyNotFoundException
```

After:
```csharp
if (!catalogItems.TryGetValue(item.ProductId, out var catalogItem))
{
    logger.LogWarning("Basket item with ProductId {ProductId} not found in catalog and will be skipped", item.ProductId);
    continue;
}
```

This defensive approach allows the system to continue functioning when data inconsistencies occur across microservices, avoiding the need for distributed transaction coordination.
